skill.name: documentation-writer
skill.description: Creates clear software tutorials, how-to guides, reference material, and explanations using the Diátaxis framework.
skill.summary: Plan and write user-focused software documentation for each Diátaxis document type.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: The skill contains prompt guidance for technical writing and no executable network operation. The Diátaxis website URL is a framework citation, not a request target or data transfer mechanism.

static_findings.snippet: Your work is strictly guided by the principles and structure of the Diátaxis Framework (https://diat

finding_verdicts.reason: The URL on line 9 identifies the Diátaxis framework that guides the writing method. SKILL.md contains no executable network operation, and line 45 restricts external browsing.

content.value_statement: Software documentation often mixes learning, task, reference, and conceptual content. This skill separates those needs and produces focused Markdown for a defined audience.
actual_capabilities: Creates tutorials, how-to guides, reference material, and explanations.
Clarifies the document type, audience, user goal, and scope before drafting.
Proposes a detailed outline and waits for approval before writing full content.
Writes clear, consistent software documentation in Markdown.
Uses provided Markdown files to match project tone, style, and terminology.
limitations: Requires user approval of the proposed outline before producing the full document.
Does not consult external sources unless the user provides a link and requests research.
Cannot independently verify that technical details are current or operationally correct.
Does not copy from provided Markdown files unless the user explicitly requests copying.

use_cases.title: Onboard New Developers
use_cases.description: Create a structured tutorial that leads new team members from setup to a successful first result.

use_cases.title: Document Support Procedures
use_cases.description: Turn a recurring operational task into a focused how-to guide with clear scope and ordered steps.

use_cases.title: Organize Product Knowledge
use_cases.description: Separate mixed source material into reference and explanation documents for easier maintenance and discovery.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Beginner Tutorial
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a tutorial that teaches [audience] to achieve [goal]. Include [topics] and exclude [topics]. Ask necessary questions before proposing the outline.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a new user needs a guided learning experience.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a How-To Guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a how-to guide for [task] using these project details: [context]. Propose an outline and wait for approval before drafting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when readers need to solve one practical problem.

prompt_templates.title: Build Technical Reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Create reference documentation for [component]. Cover [interfaces, parameters, behaviors, and errors] for [audience], using [provided files] as style context.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when readers need accurate facts about a software component.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Documentation Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Diátaxis documentation set for [product]. Map [source material] into four document types, identify gaps, and propose linked outlines before drafting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when planning a complete documentation system from mixed source material.

output_examples.input: Create a tutorial for developers installing a command-line tool for the first time.
output_examples.output: Proposed outline: prerequisites, installation, first configuration, first successful command, verification, and next steps.

output_examples.input: Write a how-to guide for rotating an expired service credential.
output_examples.output: How to rotate an expired service credential: confirm the affected service, issue a replacement, update the configuration, restart safely, and verify access.

output_examples.input: Explain why the platform uses asynchronous job processing.
output_examples.output: Explanation structure: the workload problem, queue-based processing, reliability tradeoffs, operational effects, and situations where synchronous processing remains appropriate.

best_practices: State the audience, reader goal, document type, and scope in the initial request.
Provide current technical facts and existing Markdown when terminology or style must match a project.
Review the proposed outline carefully before approving the full draft.
anti_patterns: Do not combine tutorial, how-to, reference, and explanation goals in one document.
Do not request accurate commands or interfaces without supplying verified technical details.
Do not skip audience and scope decisions when the document serves a specific workflow.

faq.question: What documentation types can this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates tutorials, how-to guides, reference material, and explanations based on the Diátaxis framework.

faq.question: Does the skill write the full document immediately?
faq.answer: No. It first clarifies requirements, proposes an outline, and waits for approval before drafting the complete document.

faq.question: Can it match an existing documentation style?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide Markdown files so it can follow the project tone, terminology, and formatting.

faq.question: Can it research information online?
faq.answer: Only when you provide a link and explicitly instruct it to consult that source.

faq.question: Does it verify technical accuracy?
faq.answer: It aims for accuracy, but users should verify commands, interfaces, versions, and operational procedures before publication.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the document type, target audience, reader goal, included topics, excluded topics, and relevant project context.
